newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends at second highest close ever.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends at second highest close ever.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE 100 ends sharply higher, boosted by oil, drug
stocks. Shrugs off 30-point Dow selloff at London close.
** Stares down weaker gilts, possible interest rate hike at
BoE meet starting Wednesday. Sterling holds over 3 marks.
** Strong futures, corporate earnings underpin rally.

"Every time short-term interest rates have gone up since October, people have used it as an excuse to go short equities and have been wrong," said Robert Buckland, UK equities strategist at HSBC James Capel.
"People have confidently cried wolf on short-term rates before and been wrong, and I think they will be wrong again," he said.
He added, "We have had good results the last few days...and that always helps to keep the market positive over the results period. That is setting the tone."
The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee meets on Wednesday and Thursday and is expected to boost interest rates for the fourth time in as many months.
A Reuters survey showed 16 of 23 economists expected a rise from the current 6.75 percent, to 7.0 percent, in order to cool off a buoyant consumer and service sector.
Credibility in the newly-independent Bank of England's ability to fight inflation is soothing for the stock market, strategists said, despite the chance for even further rate hikes later this year.

That perception was reinforced after UK investors shrugged off an early sell-off on Wall Street, weaker gilts and continued strength in sterling, which has hit earnings from companies announcing this week.
Sterling held above three marks in late European trading and edged back up toward its decade high of 3.0878 set last month.
Instead, sparkling profits from oil major BP highlighted this week's reports from 17 companies in the FTSE 100, with a total weighting of 27 percent of the index.
"We had very impressive figures from BP, which were much better than the market expected, and...a share buyback," one trader said.

BP shares jumped 40-1/2p or nearly five percent to 862-1/2p. The oil powerhouse reported a 16 percent surge in second quarter profit, raised its quarterly dividend by five percent over the first quarter and proposed share buy-backs.
Industry watchers hailed the profit rise as "brilliant" and "extremely pleasing", and raised their full-year forecasts and upgraded the shares.
Shares in Shell, which reports on Thursday, jumped 14-1/2p to 459p and was the third most active stock with volume of 19 million.
Drug stocks were the second strongest sector, with Zeneca Group Plc, SmithKline Beecham and Glaxo Wellcome Plc, tracking recent gains in their ADRs.
Elsewhere, British media and leisure company Pearson Plc soared to three-month highs after broker ABN AMRO Hoare Govett upgraded its rating to "buy" from "hold".
Pearson shares, extending yesterday's rally on higher than expected results, ended 47-1/2p higher at 740p.
Supermarket group Tesco Plc briefed investment analysts on its first half performance before going into closed season and its shares rose 16p to 435p.
"It's seen as a defensive sector and no bad news is good news," said one retail analyst.
Shares in National Westminster Bank extended their losses by the close, falling 37p to 833p.

The group reported that first half, pre-tax profits from continuing operations, excluding a charge of 106 million stg, rose to 775 million stg, from 662 million a year ago. Analyst forecasts had been mostly in a range between 757 million stg and 770 million.
Natwest disappointed some investors by ruling out major acquisitions or a merger.
Shares in BAA Plc jumped 17-1/2p to 578, after the UK airport management group said its first quarter profits rose to 136.0 million stg, as expected, from 130.0 million stg a year ago.

The most active stock was British Telecommunications Plc, with 58 million shares traded. A late ADR trade in the U.S. on Monday and a broker-to-broker trade in London dented the shares, which fell 7-1/2p to 416-1/2p.
On Wednesday, earnings results are slated for GKN Plc, Prudential Corp, Commercial Union, Cadbury Schweppes, and Standard Chartered Plc.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366
